title: Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation
hook: Distillation needs a teacher who knows more than the student. This paper gets that gap for free — not by informing the teacher, but by blinding the student.
key_points: On-policy distillation depends on teacher-student asymmetry, usually bought with a bigger teacher or privileged info like reference answers or ground-truth regions.
S²VOPD inverts the trick: same model, but the student sees a strongly augmented view while the teacher sees the original image.
No annotations, no rewards, no separate stronger model — the augmentation gap alone supplies the learning signal.
All four augmentation families they tested helped, while symmetric self-distillation (same view both sides) actively hurt.
Augmentation strength has a sweet spot: too weak gives no signal, too strong erases the question-relevant evidence and the gap becomes uninformative.
Reported to lift Qwen3.5-4B from 70.7% to 77.4% across six fine-grained perception benchmarks, recovering 96% of what privileged-info methods achieve.
content_html: Distilling a model into a better version of itself only works if the teacher knows something the student doesn't. Usually you buy that gap: a larger teacher model, or privileged supervision like reference answers and ground-truth regions of interest. Li et al. ask where the gap can come from when nothing privileged is available — and answer by flipping the direction. Instead of adding information to the teacher, subtract it from the student.
extra_html:
Their method, S²VOPD, distills on-policy from a teacher conditioned on the original image into a student conditioned on a strongly augmented view of that same image. Same weights, no labels, no rewards, no bigger model: the augmentation is the asymmetry.

The interesting part is the design-space sweep. Three findings: asymmetry is load-bearing — all four augmentation families they tried improved results, while symmetric self-distillation made things worse; strength matters, with performance peaking at moderate augmentation; and the gap has to stay task-consistent, because augmentations that wipe out the question-relevant evidence produce a big but meaningless discrepancy.

On six fine-grained perception benchmarks they report Qwen3.5-4B going from 70.7% to 77.4% — ahead of the open-source models they compare against, up to Qwen3-VL at 235B, and past GPT-5.4 — and, holding training data fixed, recovering 96% of the gain from methods that do get privileged information. August 2026, arXiv.

related.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
related.hook: Self-distillation that finally deserves the name: no ground truth, no bigger teacher — just a model voting against itself and fixing where it was confidently wrong.

related.title: Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation
related.hook: Every on-policy self-distillation method hand-picks what the teacher gets to see. LOPD makes that privileged context a learned vector instead of a design choice.

related.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: RL post-training gets pricier as models scale, since it needs the strong model's own rollouts. Direct-OPD reuses a cheap RL run on a small model instead, transferring the direction RL moved it.

flashcards.prompt: How does S²VOPD create teacher-student asymmetry without a stronger teacher?
flashcards.back_html: It subtracts information from the student instead of adding it to the teacher: the teacher conditions on the original image, the student on a strongly augmented view of the same image.

flashcards.prompt: What happened when the authors made the distillation symmetric — teacher and student seeing the same view?

choices.text: Performance degraded, confirming the asymmetry is what carries the signal
Performance matched the asymmetric setup but trained faster
Training diverged because the KL term went to zero

flashcards.explanation_html: Symmetric self-distillation degraded performance, while all four asymmetric augmentation families improved it — the gap between the two views is the whole mechanism.

flashcards.prompt: Why does pushing augmentation strength too far stop helping?

choices.text: It removes the evidence the question depends on, so the teacher-student gap is large but uninformative
It makes the student's distribution collapse onto a single token
It shifts the images off the teacher's pretraining distribution, so the teacher's outputs become random

flashcards.explanation_html: The paper's third finding: the gap must stay task-consistent. Once the question-relevant evidence is gone, the discrepancy no longer teaches anything useful.
